# Event Types

This taxonomy defines the four fundamental event types in the EPV Framework. Each event type represents a distinct category of state change in the knowledge graph.

== Event Type Taxonomy ==

=== Creation ===
'''Semantics''': The initial instantiation of an entity or statement in the knowledge base.
* '''Definition''': A birth event marking the first appearance of an entity
* '''SMW Properties''':
''' [Property:Was created at](Property:Was created at)(Property:Was created at.md) (Type: Date) - Timestamp of creation
''' [Property:Was created by](Property:Was created by)(Property:Was created by.md) (Type: Page) - Agent responsible for creation
''' [Property:Was generated by](Property:Was generated by)(Property:Was generated by.md) (Type: Page) - Process or system that generated the entity
* '''Usage Example''':
```

{{#set:
 |Was created at=2026-02-12T20:00:00
 |Was created by=User:Ontologist
 |Was generated by=Process:AutoImport
}}

```

=== Modification ===
'''Semantics''': A change to an existing entity's properties or relationships.
* '''Definition''': An update event that alters entity state without creating new identity
* '''SMW Properties''':
''' [Property:Was modified at](Property:Was modified at)(Property:Was modified at.md) (Type: Date) - Timestamp of last modification
''' [Property:Was modified by](Property:Was modified by)(Property:Was modified by.md) (Type: Page) - Agent who made the modification
''' [Property:Was revised on](Property:Was revised on)(Property:Was revised on.md) (Type: Date) - Formal revision timestamp
* '''Usage Example''':
```

{{#set:
 |Was modified at=2026-02-12T21:30:00
 |Was modified by=User:Editor
 |Was revised on=2026-02-12
}}

```

=== Relation ===
'''Semantics''': The establishment or dissolution of a connection between entities.
* '''Definition''': An event that creates, modifies, or terminates a relationship
* '''SMW Properties''':
''' [Property:Was related to](Property:Was related to)(Property:Was related to.md) (Type: Page) - Target entity in relationship
''' [Property:Was derived from](Property:Was derived from)(Property:Was derived from.md) (Type: Page) - Source entity for derivation
''' [Property:Was influenced by](Property:Was influenced by)(Property:Was influenced by.md) (Type: Page) - Causal influence source
* '''Usage Example''':
```

{{#set:
 |Was derived from=Source Document A
 |Was influenced by=Research Paper B
}}

```

=== Observation ===
'''Semantics''': The recording of a measurement or detection event.
* '''Definition''': An event capturing the act of perceiving or measuring
* '''SMW Properties''':
''' [Property:Was observed at](Property:Was observed at)(Property:Was observed at.md) (Type: Date) - Observation timestamp
''' [Property:Was observed by](Property:Was observed by)(Property:Was observed by.md) (Type: Page) - Observer or instrument
''' [Property:Was measured on](Property:Was measured on)(Property:Was measured on.md) (Type: Date) - Measurement date
* '''Usage Example''':
```

{{#set:
 |Was observed at=2026-02-12T15:45:00
 |Was observed by=Instrument:Spectrometer-7
}}

```

== Event Type Selection Guide ==

| Question | Event Type |
|---|---|
| Is this the first appearance? | Creation |
| Is this an update to existing data? | Modification |
| Does this connect entities? | Relation |
| Is this a measurement or detection? | Observation |

== Event Ontology and Metaphysics ==

The four event types in the EPV Framework—Creation, Modification, Relation, and Observation—represent fundamental categories of change in the knowledge domain. These categories are not arbitrary but reflect deep structural features of how knowledge evolves and is maintained.

=== Event Identity and Individuation ===

Events in the EPV Framework are individuated by their type, temporal location, and participating entities. This individuation scheme enables precise tracking of knowledge evolution and supports sophisticated queries about the history of claims and entities.

=== Event Causation ===

Events can stand in causal relationships to one another. A Creation event may cause subsequent Modification events; an Observation event may trigger a Relation event that connects newly observed entities to existing knowledge structures. Understanding these causal patterns is essential for maintaining coherent knowledge bases.

== Event Patterns in Knowledge Management ==

=== Creation Patterns ===

Creation events typically follow one of several patterns:
* '''Ex Nihilo Creation''': New entities introduced without direct predecessors
* '''Derivation Creation''': New entities created by transforming existing ones
* '''Composition Creation''': New entities formed by combining multiple sources

Each pattern has distinct provenance implications and requires different attribution strategies.

=== Modification Patterns ===

Modification events can be classified by their scope:
* '''Surface Modifications''': Changes to presentation or formatting
* '''Content Modifications''': Changes to substantive claims or properties
* '''Structural Modifications''': Changes to relationships or categorization

Understanding modification scope is crucial for assessing the stability of knowledge claims over time.

=== Relation Patterns ===

Relation events establish connections that can be:
* '''Hierarchical''': Part-whole or subclass relationships
* '''Associative''': Thematic or functional connections
* '''Causal''': Influence or derivation relationships

Each relation type carries different epistemic implications and requires appropriate confidence assessment.

=== Observation Patterns ===

Observation events capture different modes of knowledge acquisition:
* '''Direct Observation''': First-hand perception or measurement
* '''Instrumental Observation''': Mediated through instruments or tools
* '''Derived Observation''': Inferred from other observations

The observation mode affects the reliability and confidence of the resulting knowledge claims.

== Event Sequencing and Temporal Logic ==

Events in the EPV Framework can be ordered temporally, enabling reasoning about:
* '''Precedence''': Which events occurred before others
* '''Concurrency''': Events that occurred simultaneously
* '''Causality''': Events that caused or influenced others
* '''Duration''': The temporal extent of activities and processes

This temporal structure supports sophisticated queries about knowledge evolution and enables validation of temporal constraints.

== Integration with Provenance Tracking ==

Event types integrate seamlessly with the Provenance Model, providing the temporal dimension of attribution chains. Each event type corresponds to specific provenance properties:
* Creation events map to "Was created by" and "Was generated by" properties
* Modification events map to "Was modified by" and "Was revised on" properties
* Relation events map to "Was derived from" and "Was influenced by" properties
* Observation events map to "Was observed by" and "Was measured on" properties

This integration enables comprehensive tracking of how knowledge claims originate, evolve, and relate to one another.

* [EPV Framework](EPV Framework)(EPV Framework.md)
* [Epistemic Properties](Epistemic Properties)(Epistemic Properties.md)
* [Provenance Model](Provenance Model)(Provenance Model.md)
